extras.examples: adds matplotlib for the benchmark scripts

inputs.name: structure
inputs.note: one structure per invocation; chain selectable with --chain

inputs.name: topology_evidence
inputs.note: coordinate-checksum-bound transmembrane spans; required for the experimental tm_helix_axis_v2 method

limitations: Orientation is geometric. It fits a bilayer to coordinates; it does not predict topology from sequence, and it cannot correct a structure that is wrong.
A predicted monomer is oriented as supplied. Whether that monomer is the form the protein takes in the membrane is a separate question, answered by fold_state, not here.
Solvent accessibility is computed on the coordinates given. It is not antibody accessibility on an intact cell.
The thickness prior is per-context and is a prior, not a measurement; two runs under different contexts are not comparable on absolute z-coordinates.
Both beta-barrel and alpha-helical orientation remain experimental; neither scope currently satisfies its external-reference qualification gates.
one_line: How does this structure sit in its membrane, and which residues face out?

outputs.name: RUN_MANIFEST.json
outputs.note: runtime, inputs, limitations, and output inventory

outputs.name: --out-json
outputs.note: full orientation result for one structure

outputs.name: --out-pdb
outputs.note: the structure, oriented in the bilayer frame
